title: Consolidate routing decision paths & regional affinity cleanup
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Objective: Reduce cognitive complexity and duplicate logic in the smart routing layer by consolidating routing decision paths, extracting a single policy-evaluation boundary, and cleaning up regional affinity mapping. This ticket targets three classes of tech debt: (1) multiple ad-hoc policy checks scattered across router code, (2) duplicated region/affinity lookups and stale shard mappings, and (3) performance regressions caused by repeated context copies and synchronous fallback checks.

Scope:
- Create a single routing decision pipeline (DecisionContext) consumed by a lightweight policy evaluator service within the router package.
- Move region-affinity and shard lookup logic into router/region_affinity.go with a stable cache and TTL; remove duplicate mappings from runtime/placement.
- Replace blocking fallback probes with async health reads and an ephemeral scoreboard to avoid repeated RPCs on the hot path.
- Upgrade policy-evaluator dependency (github.com/redwood/policy-eval) from v1.3.0 to v2.0.1 and adjust callsites for new DSL shape.
- Add unit and integration tests, and a small benchmark harness that targets p95 routing decision latency.

Out-of-scope: full rewrite of smart-router, changes to the control plane routing UI, and Dedicated autoscaling policies (those belong to a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Single DecisionContext struct captures all inputs required for routing decisions and is constructed in one place
Policy evaluation is invoked only via policy-eval v2 API; no inlined ad-hoc conditionals remain in router/handlers
Regional affinity lookup is de-duplicated: every request uses router/region_affinity.go cache with measurable hit rate > 90% under synthetic workloads
Fallback health checks are no longer executed synchronously on the hot path (verified by benchmark and tracing)
Integration tests that simulate regional outage pass: traffic is gracefully routed to next-best regions per policy with no request duplication
Benchmark shows >=15% reduction in average decision CPU and <=10% improvement in p95 latency for short requests (seq_len <= 128)
technical_notes: Key files to change: router/decision_context.go, router/policy_boundary.go, router/region_affinity.go, router/fallback_scoreboard.go
Policy-eval v2 introduces a compact DSL and a streaming result iterator; update adapters in router/policy_adapter.go
We will add an in-memory scoreboard (sharded by region) to track recent health events and replace synchronous probes with scoreboard reads + background refresh
Be mindful of GC churn when moving DecisionContext to request scope; prefer reusing a sync.Pool for high-throughput paths
Add observability: counters for policy_evals, cache_hits, sync_probe_count, and histogram for decision_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
migration_plan: Phase 1 (non-disruptive): add DecisionContext constructor and start populating it from existing handlers behind a feature flag
Phase 2 (adapter): wire policy-eval v2 via an adapter that implements the old interface; run canary in staging with traffic replay
Phase 3 (switch): flip feature flag, remove legacy ad-hoc checks, and enable scoreboard-based fallbacks; monitor for increased 5xxs or routing anomalies
Rollback: revert feature flag, adapter remains in place to allow fast roll-forward
Post-merge: run a 48h soak in staging and collect routing traces and the decision_latency histogram before promoting
